items.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013
items.q: In fact there’s a story about Vido Musso? He was on Benny Goodman’s band.

ctx.x: Yeah, that’s interesting because I think it’s also probably very useful for playing the rests. Because rests are harder to play at slow tempos. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-

Yeah. They are. In fact there’s a story about Vido Musso? He was on Benny Goodman’s band. And he was having trouble playing a phrase. And Benny said to him, “are you having trouble with the notes?” And he said, “no, I’m having trouble with the rests.” Which a lot of the kids I find have troubles with rests or even with long notes, even with a dotted half note, it can turn into seven beats. Or for two — and then they’ll just blindly jump ahead. So you have to rein people in and say you have to count. You have to…

Um hum. It’s funny because I’ll tell them to do this and that with rests, and then I’ll play in a thing like we’re doing this weekend and I’ll find that I make the same — like I should be listening to myself and not jumping in too soon, etcetera.
